frank.finding: Binary relation canonicalization must preserve sensor/prior/familiarity/authority distinctions; no new FRANK semantic primitive is justified by this parser-surface test.

clay.finding: Current stack points to G9 V3 and requires networked ClayCode workers; this run uses repo-native degraded coordination because live UnifiedDB projections are absent.

harness.finding: No H1/H2/H3 or APP acceptance implication; this is BASE parser/canonicalizer research only.

claygraph.finding: Generic binary relation form may remove lexer ambiguity for ordinary predicates, but ClayGraph hyperrelation identity, typed roles and provenance remain separate typed IR and cannot be flattened into binary syntax.

unifieddb.finding: Surface normalization does not imply physical store consolidation; work/state authority remains in versioned semantic state and execution receipts.

gwt.finding: Generic relation syntax must preserve typed causal-stage distinctions; parsing success is not evidence of broadcast/use/outcome/re-entry equivalence or emergence.

hyperposition.finding: Counterconstraint: n-ary/higher-order relation identity and role bindings are mandatory; binary relation generic form is not a universal relation model.

emergenz.finding: No emergence claim follows from parser/canonicalization success; intervention and control semantics remain unchanged.

claycode.finding: Prior E2B replication shows relation-word/identifier collision survives a minimal repair. This run tests a nonduplicate strict generic binary relation canonical form rather than another ad-hoc operator patch.
